label: First copy step (fed-back first token right after <DEL>) in long sequences
explanation: Active almost only at the step right after <DEL>, where the model fed back the first original token as input and now outputs original token 1 (recall_idx == 1). That step holds 97% of activation mass. Within that step, the probability of firing and the magnitude rise steeply with sequence length: rate is about 0.1% for L<=6, 1.3% for L=8, 2.8% for L=9, and L=9 holds 72% of mass. Magnitude also depends on which first token comes back: j and p give the strongest activations (all of the top examples are j or p, at about 4.5x lift), then 3, 1 and q. It is essentially silent in the original phase and at <DEL>, and after recall_idx 2. There is weak residual firing at the last copy steps of L=9 sequences. The rule recall_idx==1 & L>=8 captures 92% of the mass, but precision is only about 0.33 because most long-sequence first copy steps stay below threshold. Which ones cross depends on the identity of the first token in a graded way that is not cleanly captured.
